laws.rule: Mount Tai Scenic Area rules (Tai'an city government, in force 1 May 2024): visitors may not enter undeveloped or closed rotation areas, or go exploring or climbing off the routes; may not smoke, light fires, set off fireworks or sky lanterns, or burn incense or paper against the rules; may not bring fire sources, controlled knives, flammables, pets, or items with sensitive maps or slogans.

Mount Tai Scenic Area: flying drones, powered parachutes, balloons, model aircraft and kites needs the management committee's consent and must follow its conditions. The 2025 holiday notice also lists drones among items not to be carried.
Mount Tai Scenic Area: hunting wildlife, collecting rare wild plants, and taking away Taishan stones are banned.

Qingdao: smoking is banned in indoor public places, indoor workplaces, public transport and its waiting areas and platforms, children's venues and hospitals for women and children (indoors and outdoors), and in the indoor areas and outdoor seating of cultural and sports venues (article 6). A person who smokes in a banned place and ignores a request to stop is fined (article 15).
laws.penalty_signal: Fine CNY 200 (about A$42.66). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
laws.heading: 青岛市控制吸烟条例 (Qingdao Tobacco Control Regulation)

laws.rule: Jinan: spitting and littering are named as uncivilised behaviour (article 18) and are fined by city-management officers, who first give a warning and ask the person to clean up on the spot (article 36). Scribbling is penalised under the city's appearance rules, and walking dogs without a lead or clearing droppings is also listed.
laws.penalty_signal: Spitting or littering: CNY 20 to 100 (about A$4.27 to A$21.33). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
laws.heading: 济南市文明行为促进条例 (Jinan Civilised Behaviour Promotion Regulation)

laws.rule: Qingdao: setting off fireworks is banned in the Shinan, Shibei and Licang districts and the built-up areas of Laoshan, Chengyang and Huangdao (article 2). It is also banned at government offices, heritage sites, stations, wharves and airports, hospitals, schools, aged care sites, and on rooftops, balconies, stairs, corridors and from windows (article 3).
laws.penalty_signal: Fine CNY 300 to 500 (about A$64.00 to A$107); CNY 500 (about A$107) if set off during heavy air pollution (article 11). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
laws.heading: 青岛市禁止燃放烟花爆竹规定 (Qingdao Provisions Banning the Setting-off of Fireworks)

laws.rule: In scenic areas, grazing animals is banned (article 29). Carrying fire into the core scenic area, or smoking, lighting a fire, burning incense or setting off fireworks or sky lanterns in a fire-ban zone or season, is also banned (article 46).
laws.penalty_signal: Grazing: warning or CNY 50 to 200 (about A$10.67 to A$42.66). Fire in a ban zone or season: CNY 300 to 3,000 (about A$64.00 to A$640). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)

layers.authority: Mount Tai Scenic Area Management Committee (Tai'an city)
layers.process: Mount Tai tickets are limited and booked in advance, with real-name checks at the gate. Reservation opens up to seven days ahead; a ticket is valid for three days after first entry. The official channel is the 'Taishan Scenic Area' WeChat account. Visitors carry the ID they booked with (ID card or passport). Foreign visitors, and Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan visitors, book online and then have the ticket checked and activated at a manual window in a visitor centre; foreign visitors use the manual gate. Entry is limited to the booked time slot and gate. Sales stop when the day's threshold is reached.
